rules.message: service_type is not in the catalog.
rules.remedy: Use the catalog subcommand to find the exact type ID, or use lenient mode for a disclosed draft.

rules.message: service_type names a scope or boundary type, not a resource type.
rules.remedy: Declare it in scopes or boundaries, or use a resource type from the catalog.

rules.message: This type does not belong to the resource's provider.
rules.remedy: Use a type of the hosting provider; a provider is never substituted.

rules.message: taxonomy is not one of the frozen taxonomy IDs.
rules.remedy: Use the taxonomy ID shown for the type by the catalog subcommand.

rules.message: taxonomy differs from the one primary taxonomy ID of this type.
rules.remedy: Use the taxonomy ID shown for the type by the catalog subcommand.

rules.message: service_type and kubernetes.kind do not match.
rules.remedy: Use the type mapped to this kind, and set the kubernetes context on k8s.* and node-group types.

rules.message: This type has no approved icon because its redistribution rights are unresolved.
rules.remedy: Keep the native label; the renderer must not substitute a generic icon. See release_blockers in capabilities.

rules.message: This provider has no scope of this kind.
rules.remedy: Use a scope kind listed for the provider, such as resource_group on Azure or iam_project on Huawei Cloud.

rules.message: This provider has no boundary of this kind.
rules.remedy: Use a boundary kind listed for the provider; physical kinds are on-premises only, and a GCP VPC firewall rule is a resource.

rules.message: This scope cannot have a parent of that kind.
rules.remedy: Use the provider's documented administrative hierarchy; enterprise projects and IAM projects are separate on Huawei Cloud.

rules.message: This boundary cannot be contained by a boundary of that kind.
rules.remedy: Keep physical and logical containment separate; use typed relations for other dimensions.

rules.message: A network or location reference crosses providers.
rules.remedy: Use a boundary of the same provider; represent cross-provider connectivity as a relationship.

rules.message: located_in names a location this boundary cannot be scoped to.
rules.remedy: AWS subnets sit in a zone. Azure, GCP and Huawei subnets are regional. GCP VPC networks are global.

rules.message: This zonal boundary is located in more than one zone.
rules.remedy: An AWS subnet resides in one Availability Zone; declare one subnet per zone.

rules.message: The subnet and its network are in different regions.
rules.remedy: Correct the subnet's location or its parent network.

rules.message: This typed boundary relation targets an incompatible kind.
rules.remedy: Use network_member_of only for network kinds and security_member_of only for security boundaries.

rules.message: This type cannot be placed under a scope of that kind.
rules.remedy: Use a scope kind documented for this service.

rules.message: This entity lists more than one scope of a single-membership kind.
rules.remedy: Keep one: an Azure resource is in one resource group and an IAM project maps to one region.

rules.message: This location field does not apply to this type's documented scope.
rules.remedy: Global services take no location, regional ones no zone, and virtual machines no rack.

rules.message: zone_ref is not in region_ref.
rules.remedy: Reference a zone of the same region, or correct the zone's region.

rules.message: rack_ref is not within site_ref.
rules.remedy: Reference the site that contains the rack.

rules.message: The resource's region differs from its network or subnet.
rules.remedy: Attach it to a network and subnet in the same region; a global GCP network has no region of its own.

rules.message: This service does not attach to a network.
rules.remedy: Remove network_attachments; show connectivity to it with a relationship if it was supplied.

rules.message: This service attaches to a network, not to subnets.
rules.remedy: Keep network_ref and remove subnet_refs.

rules.message: The subnet does not belong to the referenced network.
rules.remedy: Reference the subnet's own parent network.

rules.message: zone_ref differs from the zone of the attached subnet.
rules.remedy: Use the subnet's zone, or a subnet in the intended zone.

rules.message: The number of listed subnets breaks this service's documented rule.
rules.remedy: An ALB or EKS cluster lists at least two; a zonal NAT gateway lists one.

rules.message: The listed subnets span the wrong number of zones.
rules.remedy: An ALB or EKS cluster needs subnets in two zones; an EC2 instance's interfaces share one zone.

rules.message: The number or repetition of attached networks breaks this service's rule.
rules.remedy: Each GCP multi-NIC interface uses a different VPC network; a Cloud NAT or Azure NAT gateway serves one network.

rules.message: Another resource type shares a subnet that this service requires to itself.
rules.remedy: Move the other resource; an Application Gateway subnet holds only application gateways.

rules.message: This service does not attach to a network, so it cannot join a security group.
rules.remedy: Remove the security group; a logical security_zone remains available as a separate dimension.

rules.message: The security group belongs to a different network.
rules.remedy: Use a security group of the VPC that this resource attaches to.

rules.message: The security group is in a different region.
rules.remedy: Use a security group in the resource's region.

rules.message: deployment_context names a host of an incompatible type.
rules.remedy: A virtual machine runs on a hypervisor; keep physical servers and guests distinct.

rules.message: A label breaks the provider's or Kubernetes' documented syntax.
rules.remedy: Follow the documented key and value rules for this platform.

rules.message: The resource and its virtual network are in different subscriptions.
rules.remedy: Attach to a virtual network in the same subscription and region; use peering to connect across subscriptions.

rules.message: The network interface and virtual machine differ in subscription or region.
rules.remedy: Each NIC attached to a VM must be in the same location and subscription as the VM.

rules.message: Azure Firewall and its virtual network are in different resource groups.
rules.remedy: Place the firewall in the virtual network's resource group.

rules.message: The resource uses a network in another project without a declared Shared VPC attachment.
rules.remedy: Add an attachment relationship from the service project to the host project.

rules.message: A project is declared as both a Shared VPC host and a service project.
rules.remedy: A project cannot hold both roles at once; correct the attachment relationships.

rules.message: A service project is attached to more than one host project.
rules.remedy: A service project attaches to a single host project.

rules.message: An IAM project is used across regions.
rules.remedy: An IAM project corresponds to one region; use an enterprise project to group resources across regions.

rules.message: This service is authorized globally, so it cannot be placed in an IAM project.
rules.remedy: Remove the IAM project; the service's own location stays separate.

rules.message: This service does not support authorization by enterprise project.
rules.remedy: Keep the grouping only if it was supplied; it does not grant access control for this service.

rules.message: The EIP and the resource it attaches to are in different regions.
rules.remedy: EIPs bind only to resources in the same region.

rules.message: This node-pool type does not apply to the cluster's type or mode.
rules.remedy: Use the cluster's own node-group mapping; GKE Autopilot and CCE Autopilot have no user node pools.

rules.message: A worker Node is declared in a cluster mode that hides node management.
rules.remedy: Keep it only if the node was supplied; do not invent managed nodes or placement.

rules.message: A provider-managed control plane is given a location or network attachment.
rules.remedy: Keep it a logical boundary; hidden control-plane machines must not be fabricated.

rules.message: This workload ownership does not follow the Kubernetes controller hierarchy.
rules.remedy: Deployment owns ReplicaSet, ReplicaSet/StatefulSet/DaemonSet/Job own Pod, CronJob owns Job. Use management for a looser link.

rules.message: This reference role does not apply to the source kind.
rules.remedy: Use volume, config and service-account references on Pods or workloads; Secrets also on ServiceAccount or Ingress.

rules.message: This property does not apply to the Kubernetes kind.
rules.remedy: Use service_type on a Service, replicas on Deployment/ReplicaSet/StatefulSet, and ports on Pods, workloads, Service or Ingress.

rules.message: An ExternalName Service cannot list Pod targets.
rules.remedy: Remove target_refs, or use another Service type.

rules.message: deployment_context places this object on a Node or node group.
rules.remedy: Use node_ref on a Pod for declared placement; a namespace is not a child of a worker node.

rules.message: This relationship kind does not fit its Kubernetes endpoints.
rules.remedy: Keep scheduling, membership, policy, storage, configuration and traffic distinct; see the model guide.

rules.message: This relationship crosses a cluster or namespace it cannot cross.
rules.remedy: Use endpoints in the same cluster, and the same namespace where the reference is namespaced.
